Description:
h2. Summary
CSRF protection is globally disabled in the Spring Security filter chain (SecurityConfig.java, line 31-32). CWE-352: Cross-Site Request Forgery. OWASP 2021 category: A01 Broken Access Control. Detected by both Semgrep and SonarQube.

h2. Findings
||Tool||Rule / Check ID||Line||Severity||
|Semgrep|java.spring.security.audit.spring-csrf-disabled|31|Medium (confidence: low, likelihood: low, impact: medium)|
|SonarQube|java:S4502 - CSRF protections should not be disabled|32|Critical|

h2. Notes
* Re-enable Spring Security's CSRF protection by removing `.csrf().disable()`.
* If specific endpoints genuinely need to stay stateless/exempt (e.g. a public API consumed by non-browser clients), scope the exemption narrowly with `.csrf(csrf -> csrf.ignoringRequestMatchers("/api/**"))` instead of disabling it globally.
* If migrating to fully stateless JWT auth, ensure an equivalent CSRF-class mitigation is in place (SameSite=Strict/Lax cookies, custom header requirement) since disabling CSRF outright removes browser-based protection with no replacement.

h2. Summary
User-controlled input flows into a manually-constructed SQL string (AuthController.java, line 77). CWE-89: SQL Injection. OWASP 2021 category: A03 Injection. Detected by Semgrep (interfile taint analysis).

h2. Findings
||Tool||Rule / Check ID||Line||Severity||
|Semgrep|java.spring.security.injection.tainted-sql-string|77|High (confidence: medium, likelihood: high, impact: medium)|

h2. Notes
* Replace the manually-built SQL string with a parameterized query / JPA `@Query` using bind parameters (`?1`, `:paramName`), or a `PreparedStatement`.
* Never concatenate user input directly into a SQL string, including for 'debug' or internal-only endpoints - these are exactly the paths attackers target first.
* Add a regression test asserting that a payload like `admin' --` does not authenticate.

h2. Summary
Passwords are hashed with MD5 (AuthController.java, line 92), a cryptographically broken algorithm unsuitable for password storage. CWE-328: Use of Weak Hash. OWASP 2021 category: A02 Cryptographic Failures. Detected by both Semgrep and SonarQube.

h2. Findings
||Tool||Rule / Check ID||Line||Severity||
|Semgrep|java.lang.security.audit.crypto.use-of-md5|92|Medium (confidence: high, likelihood: medium, impact: medium)|
|SonarQube|java:S4790 - Weak hashing algorithms should not be used|92|Critical|

h2. Notes
* Replace MD5 with a password-hashing algorithm designed for that purpose - bcrypt, Argon2, or PBKDF2 - via Spring Security's `PasswordEncoder` abstraction (e.g. `BCryptPasswordEncoder`).
* Salting MD5 is not a sufficient fix; the algorithm itself is too fast and too broken for password storage regardless of salt.
* Existing stored MD5 hashes will need a migration path (e.g. re-hash on next successful login) since they can't be converted directly.

h2. Summary
A user-controlled value is used as the host/URL for a server-side HTTP request with no validation (CurrencyController.java, line 27). CWE-918: SSRF. OWASP 2021 category: A10 Server-Side Request Forgery. Detected by Semgrep (interfile taint analysis).

h2. Findings
||Tool||Rule / Check ID||Line||Severity||
|Semgrep|java.spring.security.injection.tainted-url-host|27|High (confidence: medium, likelihood: medium, impact: medium)|

h2. Notes
* Validate the destination against a strict allow-list of permitted hosts/domains before making the outbound request - never pass a user-supplied URL/host directly to an HTTP client.
* Explicitly block requests to internal/link-local/loopback address ranges (127.0.0.0/8, 169.254.0.0/16, 10.0.0.0/8, etc.) to prevent pivoting to internal services or cloud metadata endpoints.
* If the use case only ever needs a small fixed set of destinations, replace the dynamic host with a server-side enum/lookup instead of accepting one from the client at all.

h2. Summary
A user-controlled filename is concatenated directly into a filesystem path with no sanitization, in two places (FileController.java, lines 37 and 54 - statement download and profile picture upload). CWE-23: Relative Path Traversal. OWASP 2021 category: A01 Broken Access Control. Detected by Semgrep (interfile taint analysis).

h2. Findings
||Tool||Rule / Check ID||Line||Severity||
|Semgrep|java.spring.security.injection.tainted-file-path|37|High (confidence: high, likelihood: medium, impact: high)|
|Semgrep|java.spring.security.injection.tainted-file-path|54|High (confidence: high, likelihood: medium, impact: high)|

h2. Notes
* Canonicalize the resolved path (`Path.normalize()` / `File.getCanonicalPath()`) and verify it still starts with the intended base directory before using it - reject anything that resolves outside that root.
* Reject filenames containing `..` segments or absolute path components outright rather than trying to sanitize them.
* For the upload path specifically, also enforce an allowed file-extension/MIME-type list and a size limit - unrestricted upload is a separate but related issue at the same location.

h2. Summary
An XML parser (DocumentBuilderFactory) is configured without disabling DOCTYPE/external entity processing before parsing client-supplied XML (ProfileController.java, line 37-42). CWE-611: XXE. OWASP 2021 category: A05 Security Misconfiguration. Detected by both Semgrep and SonarQube; SonarQube rates this its highest severity tier (Blocker).

h2. Findings
||Tool||Rule / Check ID||Line||Severity||
|Semgrep|java.lang.security.audit.xxe.documentbuilderfactory-disallow-doctype-decl-missing|42|High (confidence: high, likelihood: low, impact: high)|
|SonarQube|java:S2755 - XML parsers should not be vulnerable to XXE attacks|37|Blocker|

h2. Notes
* Disable DOCTYPE declarations entirely on the DocumentBuilderFactory: `setFeature("http://apache.org/xml/features/disallow-doctype-decl", true)`.
* If DOCTYPEs must be allowed for some reason, at minimum disable external general and parameter entities and external DTD loading (`disallow-doctype-decl` is the simplest complete fix when full DOCTYPE support isn't needed).
* Apply the same hardening to any other XML parser instantiation in the codebase (SAXParserFactory, XMLInputFactory, etc.) - this fix is local to one factory instance and won't protect other parsers.

h2. Summary
All Spring Boot Actuator endpoints are exposed with no restriction (application.properties, line 6), including endpoints that leak configuration, environment variables, and heap dumps. CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor. OWASP 2021 category: A01 Broken Access Control. Detected by Semgrep.

h2. Findings
||Tool||Rule / Check ID||Line||Severity||
|Semgrep|java.spring.security.audit.spring-actuator-fully-enabled|6|High (confidence: medium, likelihood: medium, impact: high)|

h2. Notes
* Restrict `management.endpoints.web.exposure.include` to only the endpoints actually needed (typically just `health`), rather than `*`.
* Put any remaining exposed management endpoints behind authentication, and consider serving them on a separate internal-only management port (`management.server.port`).
* Audit `/actuator/env` and `/actuator/heapdump` specifically - these are the two most commonly abused for credential/secret leakage once actuator is left open.
